name: Entacapone
mechanism: Inhibits catechol-O-methyltransferase (COMT) peripherally, prolonging levodopa's half-life and effect
dosing: 200 mg with each levodopa dose (commonly with every co-careldopa dose); maximum ~1600 mg/day
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity; caution with history of severe hepatic disease (monitor clinically)
interactions: Increases levodopa concentrations (may worsen dopaminergic adverse effects); interactions with MAO inhibitors and other dopaminergic agents
monitoring: Clinical response, dopaminergic adverse effects (dyskinesia, hallucinations), bowel symptoms; tolcapone (not entacapone) requires LFT monitoring
sideEffects: Diarrhoea, abdominal pain, urine discoloration (brownish), increased dyskinesia, orthostatic hypotension
clinicalPearls: Used as adjunct to levodopa to reduce OFF time in Parkinson's disease; entacapone is peripheral COMT inhibitor with lower hepatic risk than tolcapone.
indication: Adjunct to levodopa in Parkinson's disease with motor fluctuations
